body:
No exact or near-exact duplicate exists: searching DSML, DeepSeek, tool_calls/content, markup, native_tool_calling, prompt-based tool calling, and finish/premature keywords returns only this issue for DSML. The shared user-facing outcome — a tool-free assistant turn flipping the conversation to FINISHED before the requested tool runs — is the subject of the open issue #5510 (and its closed predecessor #3992), and the closest mechanism neighbor is #4540 (raw tool-call markup left in assistant text instead of being converted to structured calls). However, the requested work here is narrower and different in kind: a DeepSeek-specific DSML grammar normalizer plus a streaming filter, tracked against the already-open PR #7083 (rebase of #4845). Fixing #5510's policy (nudge instead of unconditional finish) would not make DSML tool calls execute, and a DSML parser would not address narration-only turns, so closing this as a duplicate would be wrong. Worth a cross-link comment to #5510/#4540 so the semantics and markup-parsing discussions do not diverge, but no redirect or close.

Found 3 possible duplicate issues:

1. [#5510](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5510) — Content-only assistant responses incorrectly terminate agent execution before the next tool call
2. [#4540](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/4540) — [Bug]: Tool calls return incorrect/weird syntax with Synthetic Provider
3. [#3992](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/3992) — Asymmetric handling of content-without-tool-call responses terminates agents driven by weaker/local models

These may not be exact duplicates, but the scope appears to overlap enough that keeping discussion in one place may be more useful.

_This comment was prepared by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of a user, from measurements on a real installation._

## Field report: two gaps in #7083 relative to this issue

Environment: `openhands-sdk 1.63.1`, model `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-free` via an
OpenAI-compatible gateway (OpenRouter-style routing, `native_tool_calling=False`).

**Good news first** — feature detection works for this ID. On PR head
(`586628e`), `get_features()` returns `supports_dsml_tool_calls=True` for all of:

```
deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-free          -> True
openai/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-free   -> True
deepseek-v4.1-flash                             -> True
```

So the `deepseek-v4` / `deepseek_v4` fallback in `model_features.py` is sufficient; no
special-casing needed for the OpenRouter-style prefix.

### Gap 1: the block spelling seen in logs is not parsed

The PR anchors on `<|DSML|tool_calls>` (no space, `tool_calls`). Real traffic from this
model also emits `<|DSML| calls>` — with a space, and `calls` rather than `tool_calls`.
Measured on PR head, `normalize_deepseek_v4_response()`:

| content | result |
|---|---|
| `<\|DSML\|tool_calls>` + `<\|DSML\|invoke name="terminal">` | 1 call, `{"command": "pwd"}` |
| `<\|DSML\| calls>` + `<\|DSML\| invoke name="terminal">` | **0 calls**, markup returned untouched |
| `<\|\|DSML\|\|r=terminal>` + `<\|DSML\|m>` | 1 call, `{"command": "pwd"}` |

The `calls` variant survives the `tool_calls` regex (line ~80) because `\s*tool_calls\s*`
does not match ` calls`; it then falls through to the compact branch, which finds no
`r=`/`m` form and gives up.

### Gap 2: residue left *inside* an already-structured call is not cleaned

This is the part that actually produces the user-facing failure. The model sometimes does
return proper `tool_calls`, but with the tail of the DSML block glued onto the last
argument value:

```
{"command": "pwd</parameter>\n<parameter=security_risk>LOW</parameter>"}
```

`normalize_deepseek_v4_response()` returns this unchanged (verified on PR head — it takes
the `if existing_tool_calls: return resp` path). The argument then fails the tool's own
validation, which surfaces to the user as
`Missing required parameters for function 'execute_powershell'`, or — worse — reaches the
shell and executes `parameter=security_risk`.

You can see this in the wild with `2>/dev/null` followed by the block tail:

```
... 2>/dev/null</|DSML| parameter>
<parameter=security_risk>LOW
```

So the two symptoms in this issue have different causes, and only the first is addressed
by #7083 as it stands.

### ⚠️ Warning for whoever implements the argument sanitizer

Truncating a value at "the first DSML-looking residue" is the obvious fix, and it is easy
to write a regex that silently destroys legitimate arguments. This one *looks* right:

```python
# BROKEN
_ARG_RESIDUE_RE = re.compile(
    r"</?\s*(?:\|\|DSML\|\||\|\|DSML\||\|DSML\||\|DSML|)\s*[^>]*>"
    r"|<parameter\b[^>]*>|</parameter\s*>",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
```

The alternative group ends with `|)` — an **empty alternative** — so the marker part can
match nothing and the whole thing degenerates to `<[^>]*>`. Measured on that regex:

| legitimate argument (no DSML at all) | truncated to |
|---|---|
| `<html><body>hi</body></html>` | `""` — **file written empty** |
| `git commit -m "fix <TICKET-1> parser"` | `git commit -m "fix` |
| `printf '%s' '<html>...</html>'` | `printf '%s' '` |
| `if a < b and c > d: pass` | `if a` |

We hit this in production: the model emitted a correct call, the sanitizer cut the command
at the first `<`, and the agent ran a `printf` that wrote nothing — a silent
wrong-result, which is worse than the original bug.

A regex that requires a real marker does not have this failure mode:

```python
_ARG_RESIDUE_RE = re.compile(
    r"</?\s*[|\uff5c]{1,2}\s*DSML\s*[|\uff5c]{1,2}\s*[^>]*>"
    r"|<parameter\b[^>]*>|</parameter\s*>",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
# '<html><body>hi</body></html>' -> no match, left intact
# 'pwd</parameter>\n<parameter=security_risk>LOW' -> match at '</parameter>'
```

Two properties worth asserting in the test suite together:

1. a well-formed call whose arguments contain HTML or `<`/`>` survives byte-for-byte;
2. a call carrying residue is still truncated at the residue.

### Caveat on scope

These are measurements on one installation and one gateway, not a claim about all
DeepSeek V4 traffic. The `calls` spelling and the in-argument residue may not reproduce
against the official DeepSeek endpoint. Same for the regex note — it applies to the
sanitizer approach (not present in #7083 today), not to the PR's own parser, which
handles the well-formed forms correctly.
